interest:
I study JWST observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN, especially
little red dots (LRDs), compact red sources, dust-reddened or broad-line AGN,
early black-hole growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution at cosmic dawn.

Prioritize papers about:
1. JWST/NIRCam/NIRSpec/MIRI observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN
2. little red dots, compact red galaxies, obscured AGN, broad-line AGN, and
   high-redshift black hole candidates
3. SED fitting, spectroscopy, emission lines, photometric redshifts, stellar
   masses, dust attenuation, AGN contamination, and source classification
4. high-redshift galaxy formation, reionization-era galaxies, early SMBH
   growth, and galaxy/AGN co-evolution
5. survey papers from CEERS, JADES, UNCOVER, COSMOS-Web, PRIMER, GLASS,
   RUBIES, and similar JWST deep fields

Also keep papers about AI, machine learning, large language models (LLMs),
large multimodal models (LMMs), foundation models, anomaly detection,
automated classification, spectral/photometric inference, or research agents
when they are applied to astronomy, astrophysics, JWST data, galaxy surveys,
AGN selection, or literature/data analysis.

Deprioritize unrelated stellar, solar-system, local-universe, gravitational
wave, or purely theoretical papers unless they directly inform high-redshift
galaxies, AGN, JWST analysis, or AI-for-astronomy workflows.

papers.title: A nonsingular, anisotropic universe in a black hole with torsion and particle production
papers.subjects: General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology (gr-qc) ; Cosmology and Nongalactic Astrophysics (astro-ph.CO)
papers.abstract: We consider a universe formed in a black hole in general relativity with spin and torsion. The interior of a Schwarzschild black hole can be represented by the Kantowski$-$Sachs metric that describes a closed anisotropic universe. We use this metric to derive the Einstein$-$Cartan field equations with a relativistic spin fluid as a source. We show that torsion may prevent a singularity and replace it with a nonsingular bounce if particle production dominates over shear. Particle production after the last bounce can generate a finite period of inflation, during which the universe expands and isotropizes to the current state. This scenario is only approximate: the Kantowski$-$Sachs metric is never reached and should be replaced with a more general metric that tends to that of a 3-sphere.
papers.Reasons for match: This paper is a purely theoretical cosmology paper about black hole interiors and torsion, with no connection to JWST observations or high-redshift galaxies/AGN.
papers.Short digest: The central question is whether a universe can form inside a black hole with torsion and avoid a singularity. The main claim is that torsion and particle production can prevent the singularity and cause a nonsingular bounce. This is irrelevant to my work on JWST observations of high-redshift galaxies and AGN.
Full-text inspection checklist: No relevant figures or tables for JWST or high-redshift astronomy.
